previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis and a history of hepatic encephalopathy was admitted from rehab for worsening altered mental status, hallucinations, and anxiety. The confusion was multifactorial, attributed to a urinary tract infection and medication effects from oxycodone and Flexeril, with possible contribution from hepatic encephalopathy. She improved after discontinuation of sedating medications, treatment with ampicillin for UTI, and supportive care. Her chronic abdominal and back pain was managed without opioids using lubiprostone and acetaminophen. Neurological symptoms including intermittent facial droop and facial sensory changes persisted but were inconsistent with structural brain lesions, as prior and current imaging showed no acute abnormalities. She was discharged to extended care with instructions to avoid narcotics, complete her antibiotic course, and continue liver-directed therapy including lactulose and rifaximin, with ongoing transplant evaluation.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ y/o F with ETOH cirrhosis c/b varices, encephalopathy, 
ascities, h/o recurrent UTIs and h/o GI bleed presenting with 
melena.

# Hypotension 
Transient in the ED. Ddx includes medication (dilaudid received 
in the ED) vs. GI bleed vs. sepsis.  BP improved in the ED after 
fluids and 1 unit of pRBCs. The patient had no further episodes 
of hypotension during her hospital course.

# GI bleed
Patient presents with melena x2 days and spitting up black 
material.  Concern is for GI bleed- unclear if upper or lower gi 
bleed given melena and spitting up dark material.  Guiac 
positive in the ED but with brown stool.  EGD 3 months ago 
without any varices so variceal bleed would be unlikely.  She 
already received 1 unit pRBCs in the ED. She was evaluated by GI 
who felt that the patient was clinically stable and that a 
repeat EGD would not be beneficial to the patient. Her H-H was 
trended and it remained stable. She was then called out to the 
floor. Pt had EGD on ___ which did not show active bleeding but 
was notably obscured by food in the stomach. She also notably 
had erythema of her stomach, and a biopsy was performed. H/H 
remained stable for the remainder of her hospitalization, and 
H/H was 10.___.3 at discharge.

# ___
Cr of 1.3 on admission from baseline 1.0.  Most likely ___ GI 
bleed and volume loss as above. Her Cr improved during her stay 
in the MICU with IVF hydration. Cr was 0.9 at discharge.

# Leukocytosis
Patient with leukocytosis stable from prior with normal 
differential.  Unclear if she has a new infection. She was 
placed on SBP prophylaxis but had no evidence of an ongoing 
infection.

# HCV Cirrhosis. 
Complicated by HE, ascites that's controlled by diuretics, and 
grade I varices. Her home medications were continued.

# Abdominal/Back Pain: This has been a long standing issue and 
the patient was continued on her home medications.

# Intermittent Neurological Changes
Per report, patient had intermittant right facial droop, ptosis 
and left sided weakness during last admission.  She also had 
intermittant word findings difficulties.  She had extensive 
neurological work, please see previous d/c summary. Her 
neurologic examination remained stable througout her remaining 
hospital course.

# Pysch: home medications continued.
